title: Labeled finite-family Fourier estimate
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $m$ be a natural number, and for each $S\in\mathcal F$ provide $m$ labeled samples consisting of a point of the Boolean cube and a sign. The resulting sparse Fourier hypothesis has support $\mathcal F$ and assigns to each $S$ the empirical Fourier coefficient computed from the samples for that $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
For each $S\in\mathcal F$, the supplied samples are indexed by the $m$ sample positions and consist of cube inputs paired with signs
